references.text: Jesus foresees the death of Lazarus and calls it a 'glory of God', which prepares for the direct confrontation with death in verse 14.
Jesus affirms his authority over death by saying that whoever lives and believes in him will never die, which is the theological opposite of the actual death he confronts in verse 14.
Jesus commands that the stone be removed from the tomb and confirms that believing that 'the glory of God' will be revealed is the condition for seeing the miracle he announced in verse 14.
Jesus uses the metaphor that Lazarus has 'fallen asleep' before clarifying in verse 14 that he is actually dead, to correct the disciples' misunderstanding.
Jesus states that Lazarus had already been in the tomb for four days, which confirms and specifies the claim that he 'has died' in verse 14.
